messages:
maria: Quick check-in — I ran a few traces this morning after the kernel hint change. We're still seeing tenant A starve when long sequences enter the queue, even though short-path credits were bumped. Profiling attached below (summaries)
akash: ugh. which hint? the kernel selection fastpath that pins small batches to fast kernels?
lee: yep that one. We changed fastpath threshold from 8->12 tokens and gave short lanes +15% credit boost last week.
maria: Correct. Results: short latency improved for low-seq requests (~20% p50 drop) but tenant fairness index (per-tenant completion ratio over 30s window) dipped for some mixed workloads.
dana: Can you paste the perf counters you saw? especially queue depth vs credit consumption.
maria: Copied snippets: 
```
-- sample window --
global_queue_depth: 412
short_lane_inflight: 320
long_lane_inflight: 92
credit_refill_rate_short: 1.15x
credit_refill_rate_long: 0.9x
kv_cache_hit_short: 0.72
kv_cache_hit_long: 0.34
avg_tokens_short: 14
avg_tokens_long: 192
```
stefan: kv hit disparity is alarming. long sequences miss more, so they consume more compute and hold slots longer -> queue head-of-line.
akash: which batching heuristic are we using? continuous batching with time-first + token-budget gating?
lee: yes: we do time-coalesce (max 4ms) + token-budget target per batch = 2048 tokens, but we also allow early-eject for short-path requests. That early-eject seems to favor short tenants when the system is saturated.
maria: Hypothesis: the early-eject + kernel fastpath + short credit boost makes the scheduler prefer short requests during transient overloads. Long requests end up queued behind many short micro-batches and then lose their token-budget slot when the kernel switches to a fast small-batch kernel.
dana: Noted. Any perf regression tied to kernel switch overhead?
\maria: Minor. Kernel swap adds ~0.8ms on average on our A100 nodes for context shuffle. But the bigger cost is long reqs rebuilding KV cache after prolonged waiting — observed ~12% extra compute due to KV misses when the prefix is evicted.
stefan: Could we add a lane-respite mechanism: reserve a small percentage of batch credits that only long-labeled sequences can consume? Something like a rotating quota that ensures at least N tokens/sec for long lanes.
\imTim: (typo) -> tim: I'm for a soft reservation. Hard reserves hurt utilization. Maybe percentage-based: reserve 10% of token credits in each batch window for long lanes; unused portion spills to general pool after 30ms.
akash: Also consider reweighting token-budget targets by KV hit probability: effective cost = tokens * (1 + miss_penalty). If KVs for long seqs are low hit, increase their virtual token cost so scheduler treats them as heavier but also gives them dedicated time slices.
lee: Alternatively: preemptive WV (warm-vec) for tenants with long sequences — proactively prime KV cache if we detect a queued long request queued > X ms. That reduces rebuild penalty. But it increases memory pressure.
dana: We should list candidate experiments and metrics. I'll start: 
1) Soft reserve: 10% token credits reserved for long lanes, spill after 30ms. Measure per-tenant completion ratio, overall throughput, p50/p95 latency.
2) KV-prime probe: when queued_long_age > 25ms, spawn async KV warm task (low-priority). Measure KV hit delta and extra memory footprint.
3) Virtual-cost scheduling: compute effective_token = tokens * (1 + miss_rate_est). Tune miss_rate_est per tenant. Measure fairness index and swap overhead.
4) Reduce early-eject aggressiveness: increase coalesce window from 4ms -> 6ms for moderate load to let micro-batches join larger batches. Measure short latency, long starvation.
maria: I'll run 1 and 4 as A/B on a canary cluster. Tim, can you help add telemetry hooks for per-tenant token-credit accounting and KV-prime events?
tim: Yep. I'll add counters and an observability tag: kv_prime_triggered=true/false and token_reserve_spill_pct. ETA end of day for initial metrics.
\stefan: For the smaller scope, we need to avoid new regression where long sequences get worse after the fix. Add regression alert: if long-tenant p95 increases >10% vs baseline, rollback.
akash: Also check kernel-selection churn. If we oscillate between fast/slow kernels within a batch window it causes wasted cycles. Maybe add a hysteresis: once kernel chosen for a GPU for the next N batches, prefer it unless queue composition strongly suggests otherwise.
lee: Good call. Hysteresis = 3 batches might reduce churn. We should test with varying sequence-length mixes.
maria: I captured a short trace of a problematic timeline — will drop into the incident thread. TL;DR: current configuration improves short-path latency but introduces edge-case starvation for long sequences in mixed-tenant bursts. Proposed immediate mitigation: enable soft 8-12% long-reserve + increase coalesce window to 6ms. Canary those two together.
\ops-bot: deploy-candidate started: canary/credit-cycle-sanitization-v1 -> 3271112245 by maria. :rocket:
lee: Thanks. I'll watch the dashboards. If we see overall throughput drop >5% or long-tenant p95 regress >10% we'll kill.
maria: Plan for next steps: run canary today, collect 1h of mixed-workload traffic, reconvene with numbers. If safe, stage to more canaries. Thanks all :thumbsup:
